-## Built-In Helpers
+## Helper Capability Groups
 
-Stem ships pipeline-friendly builtins for common presentation and collection work:
+Stem enforces **capability management** for helpers to reduce SSTI attack surface. Only a secure minimum of helpers is available by default; complex operations require explicit opt-in via capability groups.
 
-* `default`, `join`, `inspect`, `json`, `escape_json`, `escape_html`
-* `trim`, `upcase`, `downcase`, `capitalize`, `replace`, `truncate`
-* `contains`, `empty?`, `present?`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`
-* `map`, `filter`, `sort`, `sort_by`, `group_by`, `take`, `drop`, `slice`, `first`, `compact`, `uniq`, `flatten`, `reverse`
+**Secure Minimum** (always available):
+
+* Output escaping: `escape_html`, `escape_json`, `json`, `inspect`
+* Safe defaults: `default`
+* Essential: `lookup`, `join`, `log`
+
+**Optional Groups** (explicit opt-in):
+
+* `Stem.Helpers.Strings` — Text manipulation (`trim`, `upcase`, `truncate`, etc.)
+* `Stem.Helpers.Collections` — Data operations (`map`, `filter`, `sort_by`, `group_by`, etc.)
+* `Stem.Helpers.Predicates` — Boolean tests (`contains`, `empty?`, `present?`)
+
+Load groups at runtime:
+
+```elixir
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string(
+  template,
+  assigns: data,
+  helper_groups: [Stem.Helpers.Collections, Stem.Helpers.Strings]
+)
+```
+
+Or pin defaults in `.stem.config.json`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "helper_groups": "Stem.Helpers.Strings,Stem.Helpers.Collections"
+}
+```
 
 Selector-based helpers such as `map`, `filter`, `sort_by`, and `group_by` accept a simple dotted path string like `"author.name"` so templates can stay declarative without anonymous functions.

@@ -28,6 +28,38 @@ Stem enforces control over arbitrary Elixir expression execution via the `allow_
 Runtime evaluation APIs (`Stem.Unsafe.eval_string/3` and `Stem.Unsafe.eval_file/3`) default to `allow_elixir_expressions: false`, requiring explicit opt-in to use `allow_elixir_expressions: true`.
 If you feel forced to enable arbitrary expressions in production, this indicates an architectural flaw: business logic is leaking into the presentation layer and should be refactored into helpers or backend services.
 
+== Helper Capability Groups
+
+Beyond restricting arbitrary Elixir code, Stem also enforces capability management for helper functions.
+A template has access only to the helpers it explicitly needs, reducing Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) attack surface through **principle of least privilege**.
+
+The secure minimum (`Stem.Helpers.Minimum`) is always available and contains only essential helpers for XSS protection and output formatting.
+Complex data operations (filtering, sorting, grouping, transformation) are organized into optional capability groups:
+
+* `Stem.Helpers.Strings` — Text manipulation
+* `Stem.Helpers.Collections` — Data transformation and filtering
+* `Stem.Helpers.Predicates` — Boolean predicates for conditionals
+
+Templates must explicitly declare which groups they need via the `:helper_groups` parameter:
+
+[source,elixir]
+----
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string(template, assigns: data, helper_groups: [Stem.Helpers.Collections])
+----
+
+Or via `.stem.config.json` defaults:
+
+[source,json]
+----
+{
+  "helper_groups": "Stem.Helpers.Collections,Stem.Helpers.Strings"
+}
+----
+
+*Rationale:* In an SSTI attack, an attacker can chain powerful operations (map, filter, group_by) to extract internal state or manipulate data.
+By restricting access to only approved groups, Stem minimizes the "gadget chains" available for exploitation.
+The requirement to explicitly declare which operations are needed makes dangerous choices visible during code review.
+
 == Explicit Data Boundaries
 
 Stem preserves an explicit boundary between data and templates at all levels.

+== Helper Capability Groups
+
+Stem enforces capability management for helpers to minimize SSTI attack surface.
+By default, only a secure minimum of helpers is available.
+Complex data operations require explicit opt-in via capability groups.
+
+=== Available Groups
+
+* **Minimum (always available)** — Escaping, defaults, lookup
+* **Strings** — Text manipulation (`trim`, `upcase`, `truncate`, `replace`, etc.)
+* **Collections** — Data operations (`map`, `filter`, `sort_by`, `group_by`, `compact`, etc.)
+* **Predicates** — Boolean tests (`contains`, `empty?`, `present?`)
+
+=== Loading Groups
+
+*At the call site:*
+[source,elixir]
+----
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string(
+  "{{items |> map(author.name) |> take(5)}}",
+  assigns: [items: books],
+  helper_groups: [Stem.Helpers.Collections, Stem.Helpers.Strings]
+)
+----
+
+*From configuration:*
+[source,json]
+----
+{
+  "helper_groups": "Stem.Helpers.Collections,Stem.Helpers.Strings"
+}
+----
+
+*From CLI:*
+[source,sh]
+----
+bin/stem data.json template.stem --helper-groups Stem.Helpers.Collections,Stem.Helpers.Strings
+----
+
+=== Why Capability Groups?
+
+* **Secure by default** — Only essential helpers available
+* **Explicit boundaries** — Developers declare what power templates need
+* **Auditable surface** — Code review sees exactly which operations are enabled
+* **Reduced attack surface** — SSTI attackers face limited operations
+
+For complete details, see xref:architecture:index.adoc[Architecture] documentation.

-#### What
+## What
+
 `Stem.Unsafe.eval_string/3` and `Stem.Unsafe.eval_file/3` provide runtime template evaluation when the template source is not known at compile time. Both functions default to `allow_elixir_expressions: false`, which forbids arbitrary Elixir expressions inside `{{ }}` tags. When arbitrary Elixir expressions are truly needed and the template source is fully trusted, pass `allow_elixir_expressions: true` explicitly to opt in.
 
-#### Why
+## Why
+
 Runtime evaluation of untrusted templates introduces Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) risk. By placing these functions inside the `Stem.Unsafe` namespace and defaulting to `allow_elixir_expressions: false`, the API surface makes the risk visible during code review and forces an explicit, auditable opt-in for unrestricted execution. The false default also prevents accidental template-injection vulnerabilities from creeping in via trusted paths.
 
-#### How
-Use `Stem.Unsafe.eval_string(template, bindings)` for runtime templates. Pass `allow_elixir_expressions: true` only if the template source is authored and controlled exclusively by your own team:
+Additionally, Stem enforces **capability management** for helpers: only essential helpers are available by default, and complex operations require explicit opt-in via helper groups. This reduces SSTI attack surface by limiting what operations an attacker can chain together if they achieve template injection.
+
+## How
+
+Use `Stem.Unsafe.eval_string(template, bindings)` for runtime templates. By default, only the secure minimum helpers are available (escaping, defaults, lookup). Load additional helpers via capability groups when needed:
+
 ```elixir
-# Safe by default — structured Stem expressions only
+# Safe by default — only Stem.Helpers.Minimum available
 Stem.Unsafe.eval_string("Hello {{name}}", assigns: [name: "Nina"])
 
-# Explicit opt-in when arbitrary Elixir is required and source is trusted
-Stem.Unsafe.eval_string("{{a + b}}", [assigns: [a: 1, b: 2]], allow_elixir_expressions: true)
+# With string manipulation helpers
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string(
+  "Hello {{name |> upcase}}",
+  assigns: [name: "nina"],
+  helper_groups: [Stem.Helpers.Strings]
+)
+
+# With data transformation
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string(
+  "{{items |> map(author) |> sort_by(name)}}",
+  assigns: [items: books],
+  helper_groups: [Stem.Helpers.Collections, Stem.Helpers.Strings]
+)
+
+# Arbitrary Elixir — development only, when source is trusted
+Stem.Unsafe.eval_string(
+  "{{a + b}}",
+  [assigns: [a: 1, b: 2]],
+  allow_elixir_expressions: true
+)
 ```
-Never pass end-user input as the template string to either function.
